target: A gente quis ajudar, mas ela recusou.
english: We wanted to help, but she refused.
tip: In the preterite querer marks a completed act of wanting or trying, so 'a gente quis ajudar' means we tried to help.

target: Eu estava dormindo quando o telefone tocou.
english: I was sleeping when the phone rang.
tip: 'Estava dormindo' is the imperfect ongoing background, and 'tocou' is the preterite event that interrupts it.

target: Senta aí, faz de conta que é da casa.
english: Sit down, act like you're at home.
tip: 'Fazer de conta' means 'to pretend.' 'Faz de conta que é da casa' is a warm invitation to feel comfortable.

target: Ela perguntou se eu queria ir junto.
english: She asked if I wanted to go along.
tip: 'Perguntou se' means asked whether: se introduces an indirect question, reporting it rather than quoting it.

target: Eu abri a janela porque estava abafado.
english: I opened the window because it was stuffy.
tip: porque, one word with no accent, means 'because': abri a janela porque = I opened it because.

target: Nós perdemos o voo e tivemos que remarcar.
english: We missed the flight and had to rebook.
tip: 'Perder' covers both to lose and to miss something scheduled: 'perdemos o voo' = we missed the flight.

target: Que pena, eu não vou poder ir.
english: What a shame, I won't be able to go.
tip: 'Que' plus a noun makes what a, so 'Que pena' means what a shame, the same shape as que sorte or que legal.

target: A gente soube na hora que era mentira.
english: We knew right away that it was a lie.
tip: soube is the preterite of saber and means found out or realized, not 'knew': a gente soube na hora.

target: Ele veio de ônibus porque o carro quebrou.
english: He came by bus because his car broke down.
tip: Name the means of transport with 'de': 'veio de ônibus' = came by bus, like 'de carro' = by car.

target: Ela fez uma viagem incrível para Fernando de Noronha.
english: She took an incredible trip to Fernando de Noronha.
tip: Portuguese makes a trip rather than takes one: 'fez uma viagem' means took a trip, using fazer instead of tomar.

target: Enquanto eu tomava banho, o telefone tocou três vezes.
english: While I was showering, the phone rang three times.
tip: tomar banho = to take a shower. tomar (to take) is the verb for showers and drinks: tomava banho.

target: Pega leve, ele está passando por um momento difícil.
english: Go easy on him, he's going through a tough time.
tip: 'Pegar leve' means 'to go easy on' or 'to take it easy.' The opposite is 'pegar pesado' (to be harsh/to overdo it).

target: Eu sempre almoçava em casa, mas hoje almocei no restaurante.
english: I always used to eat lunch at home, but today I ate at the restaurant.
tip: 'Almoçava' (imperfeito, habitual) + 'almocei' (perfeito, today's specific event). Habit vs. single action.

target: A gente torceu para o Flamengo.
english: We cheered for Flamengo.
tip: 'Torcer para' means to root for/cheer for a team. Flamengo is Brazil's most popular soccer team, with fans across the entire country.

target: Vocês provaram a feijoada?
english: Did you try the feijoada?
tip: Feijoada is Brazil's national dish – a rich black bean stew with pork. Traditionally served on Wednesdays and Saturdays.

target: A gente curtiu muito a praia.
english: We really enjoyed the beach.
tip: 'Curtir' is informal Brazilian for enjoy or have fun, so 'curtiu a praia' means enjoyed the beach.

target: Ele terminou o relatório a tempo.
english: He finished the report on time.
tip: 'A tempo' means just in time, while 'no prazo' means by the deadline, so 'terminou a tempo' means finished with time to spare.

target: Nós dividimos a pizza entre quatro.
english: We split the pizza among four.
tip: For this -ir verb the nós form is the same in present and past, so 'dividimos' can mean we split or we are splitting.

target: A gente fez amizade com os vizinhos.
english: We became friends with the neighbors.
tip: Portuguese makes friendship rather than becomes friends, so 'fez amizade com' means became friends with.

target: Vocês experimentaram o açaí daqui?
english: Did you try the açaí from here?
tip: 'Experimentar' looks like experiment but means to try, especially food, so 'experimentaram o açaí' means did you try the açaí.

target: Nós viemos de taxi porque choveu.
english: We came by taxi because it rained.
tip: Don't confuse 'viemos' (we came) with vimos (we saw); they are different verbs that sound close.

target: A gente combinou de se encontrar no shopping.
english: We arranged to meet at the mall.
tip: 'Combinar de' plus an infinitive means to arrange or agree to, so 'combinou de se encontrar' means arranged to meet.

target: Eu soube da notícia pelo jornal.
english: I found out the news through the newspaper.
tip: In the preterite saber shifts to found out, so 'soube da notícia' means I found out the news, not I already knew it.

target: Vocês deram uma olhada no projeto?
english: Did you take a look at the project?
tip: 'Dar uma olhada' is literally to give a look and means to take a look, so 'deram uma olhada' means did you take a look.

target: Nós voltamos de viagem ontem à noite.
english: We came back from the trip last night.
tip: 'Voltamos' is both present and past for this verb; here 'ontem' is what tells you it means we came back yesterday.

target: A gente viajou para Minas Gerais no feriado.
english: We traveled to Minas Gerais on the holiday.
tip: 'A gente' means we but takes third-person singular: 'a gente viajou', never viajamos.

target: A gente pôde descansar no final de semana.
english: We were able to rest on the weekend.
tip: 'Poder' past: a gente pôde. Note the circumflex: 'pôde' (past) vs. 'pode' (present).

target: A gente quis ir, mas não deu.
english: We wanted to go, but it didn't work out.
tip: 'Não deu' is extremely common Brazilian Portuguese for 'it didn't work out' or 'it wasn't possible.' Short for 'não deu certo.'

target: Eu fui o primeiro a chegar na festa.
english: I was the first to arrive at the party.
tip: Here 'fui' comes from 'ser' (to be), not 'ir' (to go). 'Eu fui o primeiro' = I was the first. Context clarifies.

target: Eu não sabia nadar quando era pequeno.
english: I didn't know how to swim when I was young.
tip: sabia is the ongoing 'knew' (I knew how to swim); soube would mean 'found out' at one moment.
